name: Yoshida Trail
summary: The most popular way up Mount Fuji and the one with the most mountain huts: switchbacks of volcanic gravel from the Fuji Subaru Line 5th Station to the crater rim, and a separate trail back down.

details.route: Fuji Subaru Line 5th Station (2,305 m) to the summit, down by the Yoshida descent trail
details.duration: 6 h 10 min up, 3 h 35 min down
details.permit: 2026 season rules (July 1 to September 10, 2026, now ended): a Yamanashi hiking fee of 4,000 yen per person per climb, payable in advance through the prefecture's online reservation (optional, open up to the day of the climb). The gate was closed to new climbers from 2 pm to 3 am and once 4,000 climbers had passed that day; hut guests could still go through. Rules for 2027 had not been announced when we checked.
details.gettingThere: Fuji Kyuko climbing buses from Fujikawaguchiko Station and Mt. Fuji Station. In peak season the Fuji Subaru Line is closed to private cars (2026: July 3, 6 pm, to September 10, 6 pm); park at Fujisan Parking and take the shuttle bus.
tips: It gets very crowded where the Subashiri Trail joins at the Original 8th Station, and above the 9th Station the path is narrow and rocky, with falling stones.
On the way down, follow the yellow signs at the fork near the 8th Station, or you may end up on the Subashiri side.
The descent has few huts and toilets, and some toilets may close from late August.

name: Subashiri Trail
summary: A quieter start through forest on the east side of Mount Fuji, then volcanic sand and rock up to where it joins the Yoshida Trail, with its own sandy descent trail back down.

details.route: Subashiri Trail 5th Station (2,000 m) to the summit, down by the Subashiri descent trail
details.duration: 6 h 25 min up, 3 h 20 min down
details.permit: 2026 season rules (July 1 to September 10, 2026, now ended): a Shizuoka hiking fee of 4,000 yen per person per climb. You registered in advance in the Shizuoka FUJI NAVI app (or on site, about 30 minutes) and completed a short e-learning course on rules and manners with a quiz to get your entry pass. Entering between 2 pm and 3 am needed a mountain hut booking. The prefecture's page did not list a daily limit. Rules for 2027 had not been announced when we checked.
details.gettingThere: Fujikyu Mobility climbing buses from Gotemba Station and Shin-Matsuda Station. The Fuji-azami Line is closed to private cars during the climbing season (2026: July 1 to September 10); park for free at Subashiri Multipurpose Plaza and take the paid shuttle or a taxi.
tips: Rocky ground and loose gravel become more common around the 7th Station, and the trail is very crowded where it joins the Yoshida Trail at the Original 8th Station.
On the way down, look for the red signs at the Edoya fork near the 8th Station to stay on the Subashiri descent.
There is a first-aid center at the 5th Station, inside the Subashiri Information Center.

name: Gotemba Trail
summary: The longest and emptiest way up Mount Fuji, starting low at 1,440 m with few huts, and coming down a long, fast slope of volcanic sand.

details.route: Gotemba Trail New 5th Station (1,440 m) to the summit, down by the Gotemba descent trail
details.duration: 8 h 40 min up, 3 h 30 min down
details.permit: 2026 season rules (July 10 to September 10, 2026, now ended): a Shizuoka hiking fee of 4,000 yen per person per climb. You registered in advance in the Shizuoka FUJI NAVI app (or on site, about 30 minutes) and completed a short e-learning course on rules and manners with a quiz to get your entry pass. Entering between 2 pm and 3 am needed a mountain hut booking. The prefecture's page did not list a daily limit. Rules for 2027 had not been announced when we checked.
details.gettingThere: Fujikyu Mobility climbing buses from Gotemba Station (JR Gotemba Line). This is the only trail without private car restrictions: there is a free parking lot for about 450 cars at the New 5th Station.
tips: There are few mountain huts and no first-aid center on this trail, so carry enough water, food and warm clothes.
Near the 8th Station you may need your hands to climb over piles of lava rock; watch for falling stones.
For the long sandy descent, the official site suggests gaiters, a mask and sunglasses. Toilets and huts on the descent may close from late August.

name: Fujinomiya Trail
summary: The shortest way to the top of Mount Fuji, starting highest at 2,400 m on the south side. It is steep and rocky, and you go up and down the same path.

details.route: Fujinomiya Trail 5th Station (2,400 m) to the summit and back the same way
details.duration: 5 h 10 min up, 2 h 40 min down
details.permit: 2026 season rules (July 10 to September 10, 2026, now ended): a Shizuoka hiking fee of 4,000 yen per person per climb. You registered in advance in the Shizuoka FUJI NAVI app (or on site, about 30 minutes) and completed a short e-learning course on rules and manners with a quiz to get your entry pass. Entering between 2 pm and 3 am needed a mountain hut booking. The prefecture's page did not list a daily limit. Rules for 2027 had not been announced when we checked.
details.gettingThere: Fuji Kyuko climbing buses from Mishima, Shin-Fuji, Fuji and Fujinomiya stations. The Fuji Skyline is closed to private cars during the climbing season (2026: July 10, 9 am, to September 10, 6 pm); park at Mizugatsuka Parking and take the paid shuttle. In heavy rain the Skyline closes and the shuttle does not run.
tips: Short does not mean easy: above the 7th Station the trail gets rougher and steeper, with falling stones.
The way down is steep and slippery in places and hard on the knees; walking poles help.
The first-aid center is at the 8th Station (in 2026 it was open from July 17 to September 4).

name: Angels Landing
summary: A steep climb from the Grotto up the West Rim Trail to Scout Lookout, then a narrow sandstone ridge with chains to hold, sheer drop-offs on both sides and wide views over Zion Canyon. The final ridge needs a permit.

details.route: The Grotto (shuttle stop 6) up the West Rim Trail to Scout Lookout, then the 0.5-mile Angels Landing Trail along the ridge to the top, and back the same way
details.permit: Rules as published for 2026 (checked October 2026): everyone going beyond Scout Lookout onto the Angels Landing ridge needs a permit; the walk to Scout Lookout itself does not. Permits come from two lotteries on Recreation.gov. The seasonal lottery for 2026 hike dates opened on February 13 (spring), April 1 (summer), July 1 (fall) and October 1 (winter, December 1, 2026 to February 28, 2027). The day-before lottery takes applications from 12:01 am to 3 pm Mountain Time the day before your hike, with results after 4 pm. Each application costs $6 (non-refundable) plus $3 per person and covers up to 6 people. Your permit time applies at the Grotto.
details.gettingThere: From March through November, most Zion Canyon hikes can only be reached by the free park shuttle, and the Zion Canyon Scenic Drive is closed to private vehicles while the shuttle runs. Board at the Zion Canyon Visitor Center and get off at the Grotto. You still need a park entrance fee or pass.
tips: The ridge is less than 3 ft (1 m) wide in many places, with drop-offs of up to 1,000 ft on each side. Chains serve as handrails on several sections; watch your footing at all times.
Much of the ridge is only wide enough for one person, so expect to wait and give way to other hikers.
If you have no permit, Scout Lookout (about 2.25 miles from the Grotto and roughly 1,000 ft higher) is a worthwhile turnaround point with views of its own.
There are restrooms at the Grotto and at Scout Lookout.

name: The Narrows (bottom-up)
summary: Walk upstream in the Virgin River itself, between canyon walls about 1,000 ft tall. Start on the paved Riverside Walk, then wade as far as you like, up to Big Spring. No permit is needed for this bottom-up hike.

details.route: Temple of Sinawava (shuttle stop 9) along the 1-mile Riverside Walk, then upstream in the Virgin River as far as Big Spring, and back the same way
details.permit: No permit is needed to hike upstream from the Temple of Sinawava as far as Big Spring. Rules as published for 2026 (checked October 2026): the 16-mile top-down hike from Chamberlain's Ranch needs a wilderness permit. For a one-day trip you can reserve in advance (at least one day before) or apply in the daily lottery two days before your trip (12:00 am to 3 pm Mountain Time, results around 4 pm); unclaimed spaces go first-come, first-served at the Zion Canyon Visitor Center Wilderness Desk the day before. Day trips cost a $6 non-refundable fee plus $10 per person; overnight trips cost $20 plus $7 per person per night. You arrange your own transport to Chamberlain's Ranch. Top-down trips are closed when the river flows above 120 CFS.
details.gettingThere: Take the free park shuttle from the Zion Canyon Visitor Center to the Temple of Sinawava, the last stop (stop 9). The Zion Canyon Scenic Drive is closed to private vehicles during the shuttle season. Check the time of the last shuttle out before you start.
tips: The Narrows closes to all travel when the river flows above 150 CFS, and whenever the National Weather Service issues a Flash Flood Warning; it stays closed for at least two hours after a warning is lifted. Check the forecast and current flow before you go.
Flash floods can happen at any time, and flash flood warnings are common in the monsoon season, July to September.
Wear closed-toe shoes and carry a sturdy hiking stick for the slick, uneven rocks; sandals, crocs and bare feet are not appropriate. The park does not sell or rent gear.
You can explore the first quarter mile of Orderville Canyon, a side canyon, but upstream travel beyond that is not allowed.
Even an hour in the river is worthwhile; turn around whenever you like.

name: Lake Agnes and Plain of Six Glaciers
summary: A loop above Lake Louise that links two classic trails and their seasonal tea houses: up to Lake Agnes beneath tall peaks, across the Highline Trail, and on to the Plain of Six Glaciers before returning along the lakeshore.

details.route: Lake Louise Lakeshore to Lake Agnes, across the Highline Trail to the Plain of Six Glaciers Trail, and back to Lake Louise Lakeshore
details.permit: No trail permit is needed, but you need a national park pass to visit Banff; shuttle tickets do not include park entry. Checked October 2026.
details.gettingThere: As published for 2026 (checked October 2026): the Parks Canada shuttle to Lake Louise Lakeshore ran from May 15 to October 12, reservation only, from the Lake Louise Park and Ride at the Lake Louise Ski Resort (free parking for shuttle holders). Fares were CA$12.75 per adult, CA$6 per senior and CA$4 per youth, plus a CA$3.50 online reservation fee. Parking at the Lakeshore cost CA$42 per vehicle per day in the same period and often fills before sunrise. Roam Transit Route 8X runs from the town of Banff to Lake Louise year-round.
tips: The tea houses at Lake Agnes and the Plain of Six Glaciers are privately run and open from mid-May until just after Canadian Thanksgiving in mid-October.
These trails cross avalanche terrain: Parks Canada advises against hiking them from November to mid-May, and in May and June you should check the trail report before you go.
From Lake Agnes you can add a side trip to the Little Beehive (0.9 km one way) or the Big Beehive (1.5 km one way) for views over Lake Louise.
Lake Louise is extremely busy from May through October, especially on holidays and weekends; have a backup plan.

name: Larch Valley and Sentinel Pass
summary: From Moraine Lake, switchbacks climb into a larch forest high above the lake, past the Minnestimma Lakes, then steeply up to Sentinel Pass at 2,611 m, a high point between Larch Valley and Paradise Valley.

details.route: Moraine Lake (trail starts just past Moraine Lake Lodge) through Larch Valley and past the Minnestimma Lakes to Sentinel Pass, and back the same way
details.permit: No trail permit is needed, but you need a national park pass to visit Banff; shuttle tickets do not include park entry. Parks Canada often puts a restriction on the Larch Valley and Sentinel Pass trails in summer to protect grizzly bears: while it is in effect you must hike in a tight group of four or more. Check current bulletins before you go. Checked October 2026.
details.gettingThere: Moraine Lake Road is closed to personal vehicles year-round. As published for 2026 (checked October 2026): the Parks Canada shuttle to Moraine Lake ran from June 1 to October 12 (weather permitting), reservation only, from the Lake Louise Park and Ride at the Lake Louise Ski Resort. Fares were CA$12.75 per adult, CA$6 per senior and CA$4 per youth, plus a CA$3.50 online reservation fee. Roam Transit Reservable Super Pass holders could also ride the Lake Connector shuttle.
tips: Larch season (weekends in September) is one of the busiest times at Moraine Lake; book the shuttle early.
The trail is exposed to avalanche hazard, and Parks Canada does not recommend it from mid-October to mid-June.
The alpine vegetation in Larch Valley is fragile; stay on the trail.
Turning around in Larch Valley (4.5 km one way, 570 m gain, 3.5–4 h return) makes a shorter, moderate hike.

name: W Trek
summary: The park's classic multi-day trek: up to the granite towers at Base Torres, into the French Valley below Paine Grande, and out to Grey Glacier, sleeping in booked refugios or campsites along the way.

details.route: Hotel Las Torres to Paine Grande via Los Cuernos and Italiano, with out-and-back legs to Mirador Base Torres, Mirador Británico in the French Valley, and Grey
details.permit: 2026–27 season rules (checked October 2026): buy your park entry online at pasesparques.cl at least 24 hours before you arrive. CONAF's 2026 price list gives 32,400 Chilean pesos for a foreign adult day pass and 48,500 for a stay of more than two days. Every night on the W must be booked in advance at the refugios and campsites run by Las Torres Patagonia or Vértice Patagonia; without a booking you cannot enter the mountain area. The winter rule requiring an accredited guide (April 27 to September 15, 2026) no longer applies.
details.gettingThere: Four bus companies run from Puerto Natales to Laguna Amarga, Pudeto and the park administration, leaving at 7:30 and 14:30. Puerto Natales is 250 km by paved road from Punta Arenas. From Paine Grande at the end, cross Lago Pehoé by boat or walk 17 km to the park administration.
tips: Register at every ranger station you reach; it is mandatory.
CONAF lists the climb from Guardería Torres to Mirador Base Torres (1.4 km, about 1 hour) as demanding, along a glacial moraine. The 5.4 km from Italiano to Mirador Británico is also rated demanding.
After heavy rain or snowmelt, rivers rise quickly. Do not try to cross if the water is above your knees.
There is no phone or internet signal on the park's interior trails, and the weather changes fast, so carry layers for rain, wind and snow.
The distance here adds up CONAF's official segment lengths for this route. Las Torres Patagonia's accommodation season for the W runs from September 15 to April 26.

name: O Circuit (Paine Massif Circuit)
summary: The full loop around the Paine Massif: the quieter north side through Serón, Dickson and Los Perros, over the John Gardner Pass above Grey Glacier, then back along the W. Closed until at least October 31, 2026.

details.route: One-way loop from Hotel Las Torres via Serón, Dickson, Los Perros, Paso, Grey, Paine Grande, Italiano and Los Cuernos, back to Hotel Las Torres
details.permit: 2026–27 season rules (checked October 2026): CONAF has closed the circuit until at least October 31, 2026. It will decide on reopening based on weather and safety and announce it through its official channels. At the last reopening (December 2025), CONAF capped the circuit at 100 people a day, made it one-way only, and required registration at Guardería Coirón. Park entry must be bought at pasesparques.cl at least 24 hours ahead, and every night must be booked with Las Torres Patagonia or Vértice Patagonia.
details.gettingThere: Four bus companies run from Puerto Natales to Laguna Amarga, Pudeto and the park administration, leaving at 7:30 and 14:30. Puerto Natales is 250 km by paved road from Punta Arenas.
tips: Check CONAF and Pases Parques before you book. After a fatal incident on November 17, 2025, CONAF closed the circuit and has reopened and closed it again since then. The Serón–Dickson, Dickson–Los Perros, Los Perros–Paso and Paso–Grey stretches are closed in winter.
CONAF rates Los Perros to Paso (8 km, about 6 hours, over the pass) and Paso to Grey (7 km, about 5 hours) as demanding. Between Grey and Paso there are two suspension bridges more than 20 m high.
Register at every ranger station, and at Los Perros and Paso also register when you leave.
After heavy rain or snowmelt, rivers rise quickly. Do not try to cross if the water is above your knees. There is no phone signal on the interior trails.

The distance here adds up CONAF's official segment lengths for the loop. Side trips to Mirador Británico (10.8 km return from Italiano) and Mirador Base Torres (18.8 km return from Hotel Las Torres) are extra.

name: Laguna de los Tres
summary: The classic day hike from El Chaltén: through forest past Laguna Capri and the Poincenot campsite, then a very steep last climb to a glacial lake right below Cerro Fitz Roy.

details.route: Fitz Roy trailhead in El Chaltén to Laguna de los Tres via Laguna Capri or the Fitz Roy viewpoint and the Poincenot campsite, back the same way
details.permit: Rules in force from June 1, 2026 (checked October 2026): entry to Los Glaciares through the El Chaltén gate is paid. The general rate is 50,000 Argentine pesos for a day pass, 100,000 for a 3-day Flexipass and 175,500 for a 7-day Flexipass (Argentine residents pay less). Buy online at ventaweb.apn.gob.ar. If you camp at Laguna Capri or Poincenot, you must book; these campsites are run by the Asociación Amigos del Parque Nacional Los Glaciares.
details.gettingThere: El Chaltén is 213 km by road from El Calafate. The National Parks Visitor Center is just before you enter the village. From there it is about 2 km (20 minutes) to the start of the Fitz Roy trail at the north end of town.
tips: The official brochure calls the trail very steep and dangerous when it is windy or rainy. Most of the climb comes in the last 2 km from Poincenot to the lake.
Plan your time so you are back in the village before dark. The weather in town is different from the weather in the mountains, and there is little or no phone signal.
From May to September the trails have ice, mud and snow, and crampons and poles are mandatory.
No fires anywhere in the park, no pets and no drones. Gas stoves are allowed only in designated camping areas, and you carry all your rubbish back to town.

name: Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port to Pamplona
summary: The opening days of the Camino Francés: a long climb over the Pyrenees from France to Roncesvalles, then down through the Navarre valleys via Zubiri to Pamplona.

details.route: Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port over the Pyrenees to Roncesvalles (Orreaga), then via Zubiri to Pamplona
details.permit: No permit needed. Carry a Credencial (pilgrim passport) and get it stamped where you sleep; it gives access to pilgrim hostels. You can get one from the Pilgrim's Office, parish churches, pilgrim associations or hostels.
details.gettingThere: Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port (Pyrénées-Atlantiques, France) is on the regional TER line from Bayonne; check SNCF for any replacement buses. The pilgrim welcome office is at 39 rue de la Citadelle.
tips: The high route over the pass (Route Napoléon) is closed from November 1 to March 31. In those months, and in bad weather, take the lower route through Luzaide/Valcarlos. Navarre's tourism board puts it at 16.6 km with 908 m of climbing from Valcarlos to Roncesvalles.
Navarre's tourism board rates the Pyrenees crossing as hard, so plan it as a full day. From Roncesvalles it measures 21.7 km to Zubiri and 20.3 km on to Pamplona, both rated medium.

name: Pamplona to Burgos
summary: From Pamplona west through Navarre by Puente la Reina and Estella-Lizarra, across La Rioja, and over the Montes de Oca to the city of Burgos.

details.route: Pamplona via Puente la Reina, Estella-Lizarra and Viana, through La Rioja, then via Belorado, San Juan de Ortega and Atapuerca to Burgos
details.permit: No permit needed. Carry a Credencial (pilgrim passport) and get it stamped where you sleep; it gives access to pilgrim hostels.
details.gettingThere: Pamplona is the capital of Navarre and the end of the first section of the Camino Francés. The section ends in Burgos, in Castile and León.
tips: Navarre's tourism board measures 23.8 km (405 m of climbing) from Pamplona to Puente la Reina and 25.5 km (404 m) from Puente la Reina to Estella-Lizarra, both rated medium.
From Villafranca Montes de Oca it is 12 km over the hills to San Juan de Ortega, which stands at 1,040 m, according to the Junta de Castilla y León.
After San Juan de Ortega there are two ways into Burgos; the more traditional one goes through Agés, Atapuerca, Cardeñuela Riopico, Orbaneja Riopico and Villafría.

name: Burgos to León (the Meseta)
summary: The Meseta: the wide, open plains between Burgos and León, through the provinces of Burgos, Palencia and León and small Camino towns such as Castrojeriz, Frómista and Sahagún.

details.route: Burgos via Hornillos del Camino, Hontanas, Castrojeriz, Frómista, Carrión de los Condes, Sahagún and Mansilla de las Mulas to León
details.permit: No permit needed. Carry a Credencial (pilgrim passport) and get it stamped where you sleep; it gives access to pilgrim hostels.
details.gettingThere: The section starts in Burgos and ends in León, both cities in Castile and León.
tips: From Calzada del Coto there are two ways to Mansilla de las Mulas: follow the main track, or take the route by the Dehesa de Valdelocajos and Calzadilla de los Hermanillos.

name: León to Sarria
summary: From León to Astorga, up through the Montes de León to the Cruz de Ferro, down into El Bierzo, and over O Cebreiro into the green hills of Galicia to Sarria.

details.route: León via Astorga, Foncebadón and the Cruz de Ferro, Ponferrada, Villafranca del Bierzo, O Cebreiro and Triacastela to Sarria
details.permit: No permit needed. Carry a Credencial (pilgrim passport) and get it stamped where you sleep. In Galicia, the public pilgrim hostels cannot be booked: beds go in order of arrival (walkers before cyclists), for one night only, at €10 per person; doors open 13:00–22:00.
details.gettingThere: The section starts in León (Castile and León) and ends in Sarria (Lugo, Galicia).
tips: The climb through the Montes de León takes you past Foncebadón, at 1,439 m on the Junta de Castilla y León's figures, to the Cruz de Ferro.
O Cebreiro, where the Way enters Galicia, is at about 1,300 m. The Xunta measures 22.2 km on to Triacastela and rates it medium-high, with steep ups and downs.
From Triacastela you can choose between two routes to Sarria: by San Xil (17.9 km, mostly downhill through woodland) or by the monastery of Samos (25.1 km).

name: Sarria to Santiago de Compostela
summary: The last 100 km and more, the minimum walk for the Compostela: through Galician meadows, oak and eucalyptus woods and small stone villages, via Portomarín, Melide and Arzúa, to the cathedral in Santiago.

details.route: Sarria via Portomarín, Palas de Rei, Melide, Arzúa and Arca (O Pino) to Santiago de Compostela
details.permit: No permit needed. For the Compostela certificate, the Pilgrim's Office requires at least the last 100 continuous km on foot on the same route, ending at the Cathedral, with your Credencial stamped and dated at the start and end of each stage. Collect it at the Pilgrim's Office, Rúa Carretas 33, open every day 9:00–19:00 (closed December 25 and January 1); take a QR-code ticket for the queue. At busy times, same-day collection is not guaranteed. Galicia's public hostels cannot be booked: one night, €10.
details.gettingThere: Start in Sarria (Lugo, Galicia). From Santiago de Compostela, high-speed trains run to Madrid, buses serve Galicia, Portugal and France, and the airport is about 10 km from the city.
tips: The day out of Sarria starts with a steep descent to the A Áspera bridge, followed by the hardest climb of the stage. The Xunta rates Sarria to Portomarín (22 km) as medium-high.
Between Arzúa and A Salceda the Way follows and crosses the N-547 road several times, so watch for traffic.
From Monte do Gozo (380 m) you get your first view of the cathedral, about 5 km before the end.
The distance here adds up the Xunta's six official stages: 22, 25.1, 14.6, 14.5, 18.4 and 20.2 km.
